mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified rate hike period (p > 0.05 in t-test), or the Fed Funds rate reverts before the 60-day window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by monthly PAYEMS exceeds 200,000 new jobs for two consecutive months predicts stronger consumer demand and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 200,000 and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative despite the labor signal, or the employment increase is not followed by a 2-day volatility drop below 0.8 standard deviations.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 2% in two consecutive months indicates weakening supply-side constraints, which amplifies demand-side pressure and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or INDPRO recovers before the 5-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 305 for three months suggests the Fed is likely to hold rates steady, reducing discount rate expectations and supporting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL remains below 305 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative despite the CPI signal, or the Fed raises rates before the 20-day window.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in UNRATE turns positive for the first time in a tightening cycle, it signals labor market softening and a higher expected real interest rate, which tends to depress S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE month-on-month change turns positive for the first time in a rising rate environment
regime_hint: early stage of rate hike cycle
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the identified softening phase.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising consumer payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 250,000 jobs, without a corresponding spike in unemployment (not modeled here), creates upward pressure on income and wealth expectations that drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises by more than 50,000 each month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not positive, or the volatility spike exceeds 1.5 standard deviations above the 30-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in the goods component of the HOU index (HOUST) of more than 3% in a single month suggests supply-side tightness, which can trigger a risk-off reaction and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by more than 3% in a single month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05), or the HOU contraction is followed by immediate supply chain recovery.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of RSAFS exceeds 700 billion for the first time in a month, it indicates a surge in bank lending to businesses and consumers, which typically precedes a short-term rally in equities and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: 3-month moving average of RSAFS crosses above 700 billion
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the identified lending surge.
